hook: An obsidian obelisk, thirty meters tall and cut with impossible precision, carries one warning repeated in many scripts, some familiar and some that match nothing anyone has seen. The document asks for patience with long strings of numbers and a heavy stack of footnotes. Read the footnotes as you go; they are where most of the payoff is built.
whyItMatters: The article borrows real scripts, flood myths and historical rulers to give its anomaly a depth of time far beyond recorded history. Instead of showing a monster, it stays with an artifact and the people trying to interpret it, so the threat is felt only through inference. The scale comes from arithmetic and cross-references rather than from any breach or attack, and that restraint is the whole trick.
thingsToNotice:
Read as years since the Big Bang, the numbers in the message match Earth's mass extinctions one after another, from the end of the Ediacaran to the Quaternary die-off about fifty thousand years ago, each followed by a second date around fifty thousand years on; the very last figure is footnoted only as a possible date range that O5 Command has expunged, which suggests the next return is already on the calendar. The radio pulse from the apex repeats those figures in octal with sixty more in front, taken to be extinctions nowhere in Earth's record, and the same pulse arrives from other directions in space, so the research team pictures a relay of signal fires between inhabited worlds.

The obelisk also works like a guest book: each era adds a copy signed by its ruler, from a 'Legatus Maximus Romulus' tens of thousands of years back to Gilgamesh, Hadrian, Victoria and Stalin, and handwritten versions from Victoria and Stalin turn up in state archives with no explanation of how they got there. The footnotes quietly recast Beowulf, Sodom and Gomorrah and the world's flood stories as memories of the Destroyers, with gods such as Osiris and Iapetos listed among their dead.

The ending is a policy dilemma, not an attack. O5 has ordered the radio shielding on, then off, then on again: silence keeps Earth out of the network and less visible, while broadcasting would honor a duty to warn other planets, and for now the Foundation has chosen to keep quiet.
